title: Navigation lights and day shapes explained
lead: At night, lights are how you know what another vessel is, which way she is heading and who keeps clear. This guide covers the lights a yacht shows and the ones you will meet.
description: Masthead, side and stern lights, tricolour, anchor light and day shapes under COLREG Part C, plus how to read fishing boats, tows and ships at night.
summary: Each light covers a fixed arc: masthead 225°, sidelights 112.5° each, sternlight 135°.
Under sail: sidelights and sternlight, or a tricolour under 20 m. Under engine: add the masthead light and switch off the tricolour.
At anchor: one all-round white light by night, one black ball by day.
Green over white is a trawler, red over white other fishing, red-white-red a vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre.
